title: Sex-dependent habenular dysregulation across the continuum of stress exposure and depression severity: A systematic review of preclinical and clinical evidence.
authors: Ferreira-Vorkapic C, Coelho RR, Wiech M, Tocco F, Todde F
abstract: BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is diagnosed at roughly twice the rate in women as in men, yet sex is still routinely treated as a covariate rather than a biological variable of primary interest in depression research. The habenula (Hb), particularly the lateral habenula (LHb), is an increasingly implicated substrate of depression, but two recent systematic reviews found sex-stratified habenula data sparse and reported sex effects inconsistent in direction. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether sex-related effects on habenula structure and function are patterned by stress intensity or chronicity in preclinical models, and by depression severity or chronicity in clinical populations, rather than arbitrary. METHODS: This review builds on two parent systematic reviews (Cameron, Weston-Green and Newell, 2024; Fortin et al., 2025), extracting eligible sex-stratified studies and supplementing them with an independent, two-phase search (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science) for comprehensive coverage of sex- and stress-related terms. Findings were synthesized narratively, organized by stressor chronicity (preclinical) and illness chronicity or severity (clinical), without meta-analysis. RESULTS: Seventeen studies met eligibility criteria (10 preclinical, 7 clinical). In preclinical models, acute stressors produced modality-dependent, sometimes opposite-direction sex effects, while chronic stressors more consistently interacted with, and sometimes abolished, pre-existing baseline sex differences. In clinical populations, sex-dependent habenula abnormalities were largely absent in first-episode presentations and became more pronounced, often specifically in women, with greater illness chronicity, treatment resistance, or symptom severity. CONCLUSIONS: Sex-dependent habenula dysfunction in depression shows a patterned, chronicity-linked structure in both literatures, though the evidence base remains small and several conclusions rest on a single study. These findings are hypothesis-generating rather than establishing sex as a confirmed driver of habenula dysfunction. Estrous cycle stage, baseline circuit-level sexual dimorphism, and sociocultural confounds are identified as testable moderators for future research.

title: Effect of electroconvulsive therapy on anhedonia in adults with major depressive disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Radmard R, Panganiban KJ, Kwan ATH, Dri CE, Guillen-Burgos HF, van Bruggen FH, Bargiota SI, Ho R
abstract: BACKGROUND: Anhedonia is a core symptom of major depressive disorder (MDD) and may persist despite otherwise effective treatment. Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a widely used and effective intervention for severe and treatment-resistant depression, however, its specific effects on anhedonia remain poorly characterized. OBJECTIVE: To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis examining ECT-associated changes in anhedonia in adults with MDD. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across Embase, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and Scopus. Studies were eligible if they included adults with MDD, administered ECT as a treatment, and assessed anhedonia using a validated scale. Standardized mean change ratios (SMCs) were calculated and pooled using a random-effects model. RESULTS: Eleven studies were included in the systematic review, of which five provided quantitative data for meta-analysis. Across 132 participants, ECT was associated with a significant improvement in anhedonia severity (SMC = 1.02; 95% CI, 0.63-1.42). CONCLUSIONS: ECT was associated with a statistically significant improvement in anhedonia among adults with MDD. However, given the small number of included studies and non-randomized pre-post designs, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Future ECT studies should assess anhedonia as an outcome, while using a validated anhedonia measure.

title: Effects of treadmill exercise with and without vertical traction on gait, pain, disability, trunk proprioception, and depression in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain: A randomized controlled trial.
authors: Baek JE, Kim SJ, Hahm SC, Cho HY
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Treadmill exercise may improve gait and clinical outcomes in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain (CMLBP), but the additional effects of vertical traction and partial body weight support remain unclear. This study compared treadmill exercise combined with vertical traction and partial body weight support (VT+TE), treadmill exercise alone (TE), and core stabilization exercise. METHODS: Forty-five patients with CMLBP were randomly assigned to VT + TE, TE, or control groups (n = 15 each). All groups received conventional physical therapy and completed 24 sessions over 8 weeks. Body weight support in the VT + TE group was reduced from 50% to 30%. The TE group performed pain-tolerable treadmill walking, whereas controls performed self-directed core stabilization exercises. Outcomes included Timed Up and Go (TUG) performance, self-selected and fast gait speeds, pain intensity, pressure pain threshold, disability, trunk repositioning error, and depressive symptoms. Assessments were conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and 4-week follow-up. RESULTS: Significant time-by-group interactions occurred for all outcomes. Both treadmill groups showed greater improvements than controls in TUG performance, self-selected gait speed, pain intensity, and depressive symptoms. Compared with TE, VT + TE produced greater improvements in TUG performance, self-selected gait speed, disability, and flexion and extension repositioning errors. VT + TE also improved fast gait speed more than both comparison groups at post-intervention. Improvements in pain intensity and depressive symptoms were maintained at follow-up in both treadmill groups. CONCLUSIONS: Adding vertical traction and partial body weight support to treadmill exercise may provide additional benefits for gait performance, disability, and trunk repositioning accuracy in patients with CMLBP. Interpretation is limited by the small sample size and the inability to distinguish the effects of vertical unloading from those of harness support.

title: Prospective Multicenter Evaluation of a Novel Low-Axial-Force Colonic Stent for Malignant Colorectal Obstruction.
authors: Otsuka R, Saito S, Fujimoto N, Hanabata N, Takao A, Narita K, Kuwai T, Endo S
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Self-expandable metal stents (SEMSs) are used as a bridge to surgery (BTS) or for palliation (PAL) in malignant colorectal obstruction, but high axial force may contribute to perforation. We prospectively evaluated the efficacy and safety of the low-axial-force Naturfit colonic stent in both settings. METHODS: This prospective multicenter single-arm study enrolled 208 patients at 11 Japanese institutions between 2019 and 2022 (BTS, n = 137; PAL, n = 71). The primary endpoint was clinical success of colorectal stenting; secondary endpoints included technical success, adverse events, surgical outcomes after BTS stenting, and 12-month palliative outcomes. RESULTS: Technical success and clinical success of colorectal stenting were both 99.0%, with perforation in three patients (1.4%). In the BTS cohort, clinical success of BTS was 97.1%; no perforations occurred, and early and late adverse-event rates were 1.5% and 3.7%. All patients underwent elective surgery; colostomy and laparoscopic surgery rates were 4.4% and 87.6%. In the palliative cohort, clinical success of colorectal stenting was 98.6%, late adverse events occurred in 16.9%, and 12-month overall survival and stent patency were 46.6% and 67.6%. CONCLUSIONS: Naturfit achieved high technical and clinical success of colorectal stenting with a low perforation rate. These findings support its feasibility for malignant colorectal obstruction in both BTS and palliative settings, although comparative studies are needed to determine relative advantages over other SEMSs. TRIAL REGISTRATION: University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trial Registry: UMIN000035224.

title: Cyclothymic temperament and obstetric severity as independent correlates of antenatal depressive symptoms in high-risk pregnancy: A prospective cohort study.
authors: Jung YM, Kim HJ, Won S, Myung W, Park JY
abstract: BACKGROUND: Antenatal depression affects 12.5%-44.2% of women with high-risk pregnancies, yet risk stratification relies predominantly on obstetric factors. We examined whether cyclothymic temperament is independently linked to antenatal depression beyond obstetric severity. METHODS: This prospective cohort enrolled 161 women with high-risk pregnancies at a tertiary center (April 2020-May 2021). The primary outcome was antenatal depressive symptoms (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale [EPDS] ≥10). Primary predictors were maternal-fetal intensive care unit (MFICU) admission and the cyclothymic subscale of the Korean-validated short Temperament Evaluation of Memphis, Pisa, Paris, and San Diego Autoquestionnaire (TEMPS-A). A pre-specified two-variable Firth's penalized logistic regression with bootstrap optimism correction was used; incremental value was assessed by the corrected area under the ROC curve (AUROC), calibration, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: Antenatal depression occurred in 52 of 161 participants (32.3%). Both MFICU admission (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 3.27; 95% CI, 1.45-7.37) and cyclothymic score (aOR, 1.63 per unit; 95% CI, 1.37-1.95) were independently associated with antenatal depression. An exploratory cyclothymic threshold ≥4 yielded a negative predictive value of 87.5%; adding the cyclothymic score to the obstetric-only model improved the corrected AUROC from 0.629 to 0.821, with good calibration and higher net benefit. Symptoms persisted into the early postpartum period in 77.5% of affected women. CONCLUSIONS: Cyclothymic temperament and MFICU admission were independently associated with antenatal depression in high-risk pregnancies. Because both were assessed concurrently the association is cross-sectional; pending validation, brief TEMPS-A cyclothymic assessment may help identify psychologically vulnerable women.

title: Heat anomaly, wildfire smoke, social-material vulnerability, and incident depression in a national EHR-linked cohort: A preregistered secondary analysis.
authors: Yang S, Brown HE, Klimentidis YC, Sbarra DA
abstract: BACKGROUND: Recent heat and wildfire smoke may influence depression, yet evidence from longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) cohorts remains limited. METHODS: We conducted a preregistered secondary analysis in the All of Us Research Program. Adults with a valid index date, residential 3-digit ZIP code prefix (ZIP3) linkage, no EHR-recorded depression before baseline, and post-baseline EHR follow-up were linked to 30-day pre-index PRISM maximum-temperature anomaly, Stanford Environmental Change and Human Outcomes (ECHO) wildfire-smoke PM2.5, and a participant-level social-material vulnerability (SMV) composite. Cox models estimated hazards of first EHR-recorded broad depression. RESULTS: The linked cohort included 179,218 participants and 5484 incident depression cases over a mean follow-up of 371 days. Each standard deviation (SD) higher 30-day temperature anomaly was associated with higher depression hazard in Aim 1 (hazard ratio [HR] 1.06, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-1.10) and Aim 2 (HR 1.08, 95% CI 1.04-1.11). We found no evidence of an association between 30-day mean wildfire-smoke PM2.5 and depression. SMV had a stronger per-SD association (HR 1.36, 95% CI 1.33-1.40) than heat anomaly and was stable under stricter component-completeness rules. Heat and SMV associations were similar across follow-up periods, whereas the smoke association varied over time. LIMITATIONS: Exposure was assigned at ZIP3 level and was not updated after baseline. Depression reflects EHR-recorded diagnosis, and differential health-care access or unrecorded prior depression may affect ascertainment. CONCLUSIONS: Higher local temperature anomaly and greater SMV were associated with first EHR-recorded depression. We found no evidence of an association between mean wildfire-smoke PM2.5 and depression in the preregistered primary model, while secondary smoke analyses showed heterogeneity by exposure metric and follow-up period. The SMV association was stronger than the heat-anomaly association.

title: Breaking the degenerative triad: Microenvironment reprogramming biomaterials for intervertebral disc regeneration.
authors: Zhao X, Han X, Hu Z, Chen Y, Wang X, Liu Q, Hu X, Zhang Q
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) represents a leading cause of chronic low back pain worldwide, imposing considerable public health and socioeconomic burdens. Current clinical interventions remain largely palliative, unable to reverse the progressive pathological cascade. This cascade is driven by a core self-amplifying triad of oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and nutrient deprivation within the unique avascular, high-load disc niche, and ultimately progresses to end-stage terminal phenotypes such as biomechanical failure and neurovascular ingrowth. Over recent years, biomaterial-based regenerative strategies have evolved from passive structural fillers toward multifunctional platforms capable of active microenvironmental reprogramming. This review provides a systematic, critical synthesis of state-of-the-art advances in the field, organized within a hierarchical framework spanning immunometabolic modulation of the degenerative niche and targeted delivery of cellular and molecular therapeutics with further elaboration of precision-stratified design and whole-disc tissue engineering. We critically appraise evidence maturity across different strategy classes and dissect disc-specific translational barriers, noting that most candidate platforms remain at preclinical validation stages. Building on this analysis, we outline priority research directions and realistic near-term translational milestones to guide rational development of next-generation regenerative platforms toward durable functional disc repair.

title: A let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicle-laden bioactive scaffold promotes immunomodulation and regeneration of segmental tracheal defects.
authors: Liu B, Wei N, Liang L, Shi Z, Liu P, Zeng T, Zhang H, Zhang H
abstract: Segmental tracheal defects resulting from trauma, tumor resection, or congenital malformations pose significant challenges for reconstruction. Persistent post-injury inflammation, inadequate neovascularization, and delayed epithelial restoration contribute to the formation of granulation tissue and subsequent graft failure. In this study, we developed a bioactive tracheal scaffold for sustained local delivery of let-7a-5p-engineered extracellular vesicles (let-7a-5p-EVs) to modulate the regenerative microenvironment during tracheal repair. The scaffold was constructed by integrating a mechanically optimized polycaprolactone (PCL) framework with a 20% Pluronic F127 hydrogel, which served as a local reservoir for EV retention and sustained release. Let-7a-5p-EVs were generated from lentivirally engineered human gingiva-derived mesenchymal stem cells and showed typical EV morphology, representative EV marker expression, and efficient uptake by airway epithelial cells. In vitro, let-7a-5p-EVs enhanced airway epithelial cell migration and shifted lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced macrophages from a pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype toward a reparative M2-like phenotype, accompanied by reduced inflammatory cytokine expression. In a rabbit segmental tracheal defect model, the let-7a-5p-EV-laden scaffold enhanced neovascularization, mitigated local inflammatory responses, promoted mucociliary epithelial reconstruction, and maintained airway patency. The let-7a-5p-EV scaffold improved biomechanical recovery, and increased survival rates. Transcriptomic profiling and molecular validation indicated that these effects were associated with the attenuation of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB)-associated inflammatory activation, as evidenced by reduced p65 phosphorylation and nuclear localization. These findings demonstrate that sustained local delivery of engineered EVs from a mechanically competent bioactive scaffold provides an effective immunomodulatory strategy for the regenerative repair of segmental tracheal defects and offers translational potential for functional airway reconstruction.

title: Transrectal ultrasonographic assessment of the equine fetal distal limb beyond the first phalanx for predicting fetal age and bone development in Quarter Horses.
authors: Renaudin C, Wensley F, Morgan J, Cassano J, Spriet M
abstract: In Quarter Horses (QH), fetal age can be predicted within 2 weeks prior to 200- days of gestation ultrasonographically; however, as pregnancy advances, accuracy decreases. Recently, fetal ultrasonographic measurement of the first phalanx length (P1L) was introduced as a novel biometric parameter during late gestation, and the timing of appearance and closure of P1 epiphyses has been identified as potential markers of bone development. The overall aim of this study is to describe distal limb bone development beyond the first phalanx. Ten healthy pregnant mares (9 QH and 1 Thoroughbred carrying a QH fetus) with known ovulation dates were used. Transrectal ultrasonography was performed every 2 weeks from 9 months of gestation until parturition. P2 length (P2L) correlated highly with days of gestation (p < 0.0001; r2 = 0.75). A correlation equation was established: y = 5.343 (±0.403) x +205.1(±6.99) (y = predicted value of gestational age in days; x = P2 length in mm). Ossification of distal MC3, P1 and P2 epiphyses, and sesamoid bones, appeared in a chronological order, with the distal MC3 epiphysis ossification center appearing first, followed by distal P1, distal P2, proximal sesamoid bones, and finally distal sesamoid bone. Distal limb ossification can be considered complete in QH when the distal MC3 epiphysis, proximal epiphyses of P1 and P2, and all sesamoid bones are present. Clinically, fetal ultrasonography of the distal limb may be used to assess fetal age and bone development.

title: Postoperative infections after cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass - incidence, performance of diagnostic procedures, and predictive factors.
authors: Erixon C, Johannesson E, Dardashti A, Melhammar L, Nilsson J, Thelaus L, Linder A, Zindovic I
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Cardiac surgery using cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) induces a systemic inflammatory response that affects common inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein (CRP), white blood cell count (WBC), and body temperature, complicating postoperative diagnosis of infections. The objective of this study was to assess the incidence of postoperative infections and evaluate the performance of clinically used biomarkers. DESIGN: This was a bidirectional cohort study including patients undergoing cardiac surgery with CPB between 1st of February 2020 and 22nd of September 2021. Patients with postoperative infection were compared to patients without. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of postoperative infections. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluated the diagnostic ability of current biomarkers to detect infection. RESULTS: A total of 1,222 patients were included. The incidence of postoperative infections (during hospitalisation and/or late infection) was 17.3%. Patients with postoperative infection had more comorbidities, underwent more complex procedures, and had higher mortality (90-day mortality 3.8% vs 1.5%, p = 0.045; 1-year mortality 5.7% vs 2.7%, p = 0.032). CRP, WBC, and temperature performed poorly in detecting postoperative infection, although peak CRP (OR 1.069, p < 0.001) and peak temperature (OR 2.408, p = 0.005) were independent predictors of postoperative infection. Peak temperature occurred on postoperative day 5 in infected patients versus day 2 in those without infection. CONCLUSION: Postoperative infections following cardiac surgery with CPB remain common and are associated with increased postoperative complications and mortality. Common inflammatory biomarkers perform poorly in detecting infection. Improved diagnostic tools are needed to facilitate early detection and treatment.

title: Sustained delivery of 3D-bioprinted stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles promotes neural regeneration following traumatic brain injury via the CREB1/PGC-1α/FNDC5 axis.
authors: Ai Y, Zhang Q, Chen T, Lin L, Chen Z, Liu G, Liu J, Dong Z
abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical translation of stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) for traumatic brain injury (TBI) is restricted by low yield in 2D culture and rapid in vivo clearance. OBJECTIVE: To develop an in situ sustained delivery system (3D-sEVs@Gel) encapsulating 3D-bioprinted adipose stem cell (ADSC)-derived sEVs (3D-ADSC-sEVs) within GelMA (Gelatin methacryloyl) hydrogel for long-term functional repair after TBI. METHODS: SEVs derived from coaxially bioprinted 3D-ADSCs were isolated, and a GelMA hydrogel-based delivery system was subsequently constructed. Following orthotopic transplantation of the 3D-sEVs@Gel system into the lesion site after TBI, functional recovery, neural stem cell (NSC) proliferation and lineage-associated responses, and the underlying molecular mechanisms were systematically evaluated through behavioral tests, immunofluorescence, multi-omics, and pharmacological inhibition. RESULTS: SEVs generated using the coaxial alginate-microfiber culture system exhibited an approximately eightfold higher yields and protein loading compared with those obtained from 2D culture. In vivo, 3D-sEVs@Gel prolonged local retention, reduced tissue loss, and significantly improved long-term sensorimotor coordination and spatial memory following TBI. In addition, treatment increased the numbers of proliferating cells co-expressing neural progenitor-, neuronal-, and oligodendroglial-lineage-associated markers within the examined neurogenic regions. Mechanistically, 3D-sEV treatment increased nuclear CREB1 levels in NSCs, promoting PGC-1α transcription and subsequent FNDC5 expression, thereby supporting endogenous neurogenesis and functional neural repair. CONCLUSION: The 3D-sEVs@Gel system promotes chronic neurological reconstruction post-TBI by modulating NSC proliferation and neural lineage-associated responses through the CREB1/PGC-1α/FNDC5 pathway, offering a promising cell-free strategy for neural repair and tissue engineering.

title: Maternal piromelatine treatment is associated with attenuated behavioral alterations and sex-specific changes in hippocampal pCREB/BDNF signaling in adult offspring following prenatal constant-light exposure.
authors: Stoyanova T, Ivanova P, Tchekalarova J
abstract: Maternal exposure to constant light during pregnancy (CLE) is associated with disrupted circadian organization and persistent behavioral alterations in adult offspring. This study examined behavioural performance and 24-hour locomotor activity patterns, as well as hippocampal pCREB and BDNF levels, in adult male and female offspring following prenatal CLE and maternal treatment with piromelatine (pir), which acts as an agonist at melatonin MT1/MT2 and serotonin 5-HT1A/5-HT1D receptors. Pregnant Wistar rats under light-dark regime received vehicle (veh), whereas dams exposed to CLE received vehicle (LL-veh), pir (10 mg/kg), or melatonin. Compared to the LL-veh groups, offspring from pir-treated dams exhibited reduced anxiety- and depression-like responses and improved working memory in both sexes. Individual-subject cosinor analysis revealed heterogeneous 24-hour locomotor rhythmicity within and between groups. No significant treatment-group effect was detected for MESOR or amplitude, and the descriptive acrophase patterns did not provide evidence of treatment-induced restoration or normalization of circadian organization. Maternal pir treatment was associated with higher hippocampal pCREB and BDNF levels in male, but not female offspring relative to the LL-veh group. While the behavioral and molecular differences occurred concurrently in males, these findings do not prove that pCREB/BDNF signaling mediated the behavioral outcomes. Furthermore, the study cannot distinguish the direct developmental effects of maternal pir exposure from those mediated through maternal or offspring circadian rhythm. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted as long-term behavioral and sex-specific molecular differences associated with maternal pir treatment rather than as evidence of circadian-independent antidepressant, anxiolytic, cognitive-enhancing, or BDNF-enhancing actions.

title: Duration of post-ovulation uterine fluid in mares with persistent mating-induced endometritis predicts pregnancy rate, and earlier mating shifts fluid persistence relative to ovulation.
authors: England GCW, Newcombe JR
abstract: Persistent mating-induced endometritis commonly causes subfertility in mares. We assessed 313 natural-cover breeding cycles from 192 mares examined daily until at least day 5 after ovulation, establishing the last day post-ovulation on which uterine fluid remained detectable. Fluid was detected after ovulation in 52.4% of all cycles. The longer fluid persisted the lower the pregnancy rate: 73.8% with no post-ovulation fluid, 32.0% when fluid was last detected on day 2 post-ovulation, and 17.6% when fluid persisted to day 3 or beyond. Each additional day fluid persisted post-ovulation was associated with a 41% reduction in the odds of pregnancy. Recording fluid duration relative to ovulation was superior in predicting pregnancy compared with recording fluid duration relative to mating. Data from a subsequent cycle were available for 101 mares bred again at cycle 2 (97 that did not conceive at cycle 1 and 4 that had lost a cycle 1 pregnancy); attempts were made to mate the mare earlier in subsequent cycles. Total number of days fluid was detectable from mating was similar at cycle 1 and cycle 2 in these mares (1.88 versus 1.86 days; P = 0.77). In 54 mares the day of mating at the next cycle relative to ovulation was advanced by at least one day at cycle 2; and yet the duration of fluid persistence remained unchanged. Consequently, the last day of fluid persistence post-ovulation decreased (1.61 to 0.65 days; P < 0.001). In the 47 mares whose mating interval was unchanged at cycle 2, the last post-ovulation fluid day was also unchanged, providing an internal control for the redistribution finding. Earlier mating was associated with higher pregnancy rates across all cycles (OR 1.969; P < 0.001) but not significantly when only first-cycles were analysed (P = 0.92), or after adjustment for cycle number (P = 0.69). Persistence of fluid post-ovulation is negatively associated with pregnancy rate, with a critical reduction when fluid persists beyond day 2. In treated mares, total fluid duration appeared to be a fixed characteristic; earlier mating redistributed the period of fluid persistence to earlier relative to ovulation, resulting in fewer post-ovulation fluid days. Plausibly, earlier fluid resolution after ovulation may allow better uterine recovery prior to entry of the embryo and thus increase pregnancy rate.

title: Effect of short-term storage prior to vitrification on pregnancy rates of dromedary camel embryos.
authors: Mulligan BP, Skidmore JA
abstract: Short-term storage of embryos prior to cryopreservation may improve the logistical flexibility of dromedary camel embryo transfer (ET) programs. However, the impact of such storage on embryo cryotolerance remains unclear. The objective of the present study was to evaluate the effect of storing dromedary camel embryos for 24 h at either room temperature (RT) or 4 °C prior to vitrification on subsequent pregnancy rates following ET. A total of 60 Day-7 in vivo-derived embryos were assigned to one of three treatment groups: immediate vitrification without prior storage (NS, n = 20), storage at 4 °C for 24 h prior to vitrification (4C, n = 20), or storage at room temperature (RT, n = 20) for 24 h prior to vitrification. Within each group, embryos were further categorised according to diameter (<500 μm or ≥500 μm). Following warming, embryos were transferred in pairs to synchronized recipients and pregnancy establishment was assessed between days 18-20 and day 60 of gestation. The transfer of NS embryos produced pregnancy rates of 60% (6/10) at 18-20 days and 50% (5/10) at day 60. Transfer of embryos in the 4C group resulted in pregnancy rates of 40% (4/10) and 30% (3/10), respectively. In contrast, embryos stored at RT prior to vitrification failed to establish pregnancies (0/10). These findings demonstrate that while short-term cooling may be compatible with subsequent vitrification, storage at room temperature could severely compromise embryo cryotolerance.

title: Seminal extracellular vesicles improve cryosurvival and fertility potential of kundhi buffalo sperm.
authors: Malak KA, Korejo NA, Lund AK, Malak AA, Magsi AS, Bux R, Aqeel M
abstract: Buffaloes are important contributors to agricultural production in many developing countries, yet poor semen cryosurvival remains a major challenge for efficient artificial insemination and genetic improvement. In recent years, small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) have emerged as important mediators of intercellular communication and reproductive function; however, their potential as supplements for improving buffalo semen cryosurvival remains poorly understood. Therefore, this study evaluated the influence of adding a seminal plasma-derived small extracellular vesicle-enriched preparation to a Tris extender using post-thaw sperm traits, oxidative status, DNA integrity, HSP70 and PRM1 transcript abundance, and fertility of Kundhi buffalo bull semen. Seminal plasma-derived particles were isolated and characterized by nanoparticle tracking analysis, showing a mean diameter of 117.8 ± 2.47 nm, modal diameter of 89.4 ± 1.41 nm, and concentration of (3.21 ± 0.05) × 1011 particles/mL. Thirty-two ejaculates from four Kundhi buffalo bulls were pooled and extended with a Tris extender supplemented with 0, 25, 50, 100, or 200 μg/mL sEV-enriched preparation before cryopreservation. Post-thaw sperm quality, early apoptosis, DNA fragmentation, lipid peroxidation, antioxidant enzymes, and relative mRNA abundance of HSP70 and PRM1 were assessed. All evaluated post-thaw variables differed (P < 0.05) after supplementation, whereas 50 μg/mL revealed the strongest response. The EV-50 group showed higher total motility, progressive motility, viability, and HOST-positive spermatozoa, however reduced early apoptotic sperm, DNA fragmentation, and MDA concentration than the control group. EV-50 also enhanced SOD, catalase, total glutathione, HSP70 and PRM1 expression (1.91 ± 0.07-fold and 1.69 ± 0.05-fold, respectively). In fertility validation, pregnancy rate increased from 41.7% in the control group to 56.7% in the EV-50-treated semen group, with higher odds of pregnancy (OR = 1.83; P = 0.028). In conclusion, supplementation with 50 μg/mL of the sEV-enriched preparation improved post-thaw sperm quality, redox homeostasis, DNA integrity, HSP70 and PRM1 transcript abundance, and field fertility, supporting its potential as a cryopreservation supplement for enhancing the reproductive performance of Kundhi buffalo semen.

title: Hemodynamic effects of ventilating or not, during cardiopulmonary bypass in a porcine model.
authors: Kvalheim VL, Mongstad A, Husby P, Stangeland L, Nginamau ES, Osman TA, Yamada S, Grong K
abstract: Background. Optimal ventilator setting during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is unknown. Improved gas exchange and lung compliance have been suggested as favourable outcomes when lungs are ventilated. However, long-time effects have been hard to demonstrate. There has been less focus on the immediate circulatory effects of ventilator settings during cardioplegia and CPB, and potentially hemodynamic effects of different ventilator strategies are unknown. Methods. Sixteen anesthetized pigs on normothermic CPB with 80 min of aortic cross-clamp and cardioplegic arrest were randomized to a ventilated and a not ventilated group. After weaning, both cardiac-, hemodynamic-, and pulmonary functions were evaluated for up to 120 min. Results. Left ventricular variables and cardiac output did not differ between the two study groups, neither before nor after weaning. After weaning, mean pulmonary artery pressure was increased in ventilated compared to not ventilated animals. Neither pulmonary compliance nor oxygen uptake differed between groups in surviving animals. Conclusions. Disconnection of the ventilator during CPB and cardiac arrest did not affect lung compliance and oxygen uptake, neither positively nor negatively. In the ventilated group, a temporary increase in the pulmonary pressure after weaning was observed.

title: An optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched dual-crosslinkable hydrogel for cell-free remodeling of the corneal stroma.
authors: Wu W, Huai S, Li C, Wang L, Xie S, Lei L, Liu X, Wang J
abstract: Corneal trauma is a leading cause of visual impairment and blindness worldwide, yet corneal stromal repair and regeneration remain a significant challenge in ophthalmology because of its limited intrinsic repair capacity and fibrotic scar formation during healing process. Here we report an optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched in situ dual-crosslinkable hydrogel that enables cell-free corneal stromal remodeling. By integrating dynamic covalent crosslinking with static photocrosslinking strategy, the optimized hydrogel-based substitute achieved high optical transparency, a refractive index of approximately 1.35, and an elastic modulus of 83.8 ± 13.4 kPa, closely resembling the properties of the healthy human cornea. In a rabbit model of deep corneal defects, the optimized in situ-forming hydrogel adapted to the defect geometry, adhered stably to the wound bed, recapitulated the optical and biomechanical properties of the native cornea, and supported scarless corneal stromal remodeling. Incorporation of the antimicrobial peptide HHC36 further endowed the hydrogel with robust antibacterial activity without compromising its optical and biomechanical properties. In a rabbit model of P. aeruginosa-infected deep corneal defects, the HHC36-loaded in situ-forming hydrogel effectively mitigated clinical signs of infection and substantially promoted corneal stromal remodeling within 30 days while reducing fibrosis. Overall, this optically and biomechanically corneal tissue-matched in situ dual-crosslinkable hydrogel might be a promising substitute for corneal stromal remodeling.

Type D personality, psychiatric symptom burden, and life satisfaction in bipolar II disorder and major depressive disorder: A family-based study.
authors: Örüm D, Örüm MH, Atmaca M
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type D personality combines negative affectivity (NA) and social inhibition (SI), yet its relevance to bipolar II disorder (BD-II), major depressive disorder (MDD), and their parents remains poorly understood. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 46 participants with BD-II and 46 with MDD in clinical remission, 50 controls without a current psychiatric disorder (C), and one co-residing biological parent per participant were assessed with the Type D Personality Scale (DS14), Adult Life Satisfaction Scale, Beck Depression Inventory-II, and clinician-rated Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS). NA, SI, and their interaction (NA × SI) were modelled continuously, with BPRS scores tested as a mediator of associations with life satisfaction. RESULTS: Type D personality was present in 87.0% of BD-II, 50.0% of MDD, and 10.0% of C participants (p < 0.001) and also differed across parental groups (fathers, p = 0.014; mothers, p = 0.030); pairwise differences from C parents were significant for fathers only. After covariate adjustment, participant groups differed in NA, SI, symptom burden, and life satisfaction (all Holm-corrected p < 0.001). In joint models, NA and SI were each associated with lower life satisfaction in all groups, whereas symptom burden was associated with NA in BD-II (p = 0.031) and SI in MDD (p = 0.004), but not in C participants, and not with NA × SI within any group. Corresponding indirect associations via symptom burden emerged in BD-II (NA: -0.653; BCa 95% CI: -1.610 to -0.155) and MDD (SI: -0.756; BCa 95% CI: -1.751 to -0.217), but not in C participants; the indirect effects did not differ significantly between BD-II and MDD. CONCLUSIONS: Within diagnostic groups, NA and SI, rather than their synergistic combination, were related to life satisfaction and, less consistently, symptom burden in remitted mood disorders; Type D characteristics were also elevated in parents.

title: Screening a thermotolerant Komagataella phaffii strain with methanol cross-tolerance and the associated physiological and transcriptional responses.
authors: Li C, Jiang T, Bo Y, Lu Z, Zhou Y, Zhang G
abstract: Komagataella phaffii is a prominent methylotrophic yeast widely used in industrial biotechnology for heterologous protein production, chemical synthesis, and C1 feedstock utilization. However, its industrial application is limited by thermal stress and methanol toxicity, while the relationship between heat adaptation and methanol tolerance remains poorly understood. Here, we obtained a thermotolerant mutant ATH through ARTP mutagenesis followed by adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) under heat stress (37 °C). ATH tolerated heat and methanol robustly under individual stress conditions, achieving 3-fold and 8-fold higher cell densities than GS115 at 37 °C or in 5% (v/v) methanol, respectively, yet failed under the combined stress of 37 °C and 5% methanol. Using three proteins (GFP, OPH, and ChiA) as reporters, we found that ATH showed higher heterologous expression than GS115 at 33 °C. Physiologically, ATH displayed enhanced cell wall/membrane integrity, reduced ROS accumulation and lower lipid peroxidation (>30% reduction in MDA), and accelerated formaldehyde clearance. Transcriptomics identified 561 shared differentially expressed genes, with coordinated upregulation of heat shock proteins (HSP70/40/90 families; Hsp104 and Hsp70-SSA2), antioxidant enzymes (catalase, peroxiredoxin), and cell wall/membrane remodeling genes, alongside downregulation of amino acid and secondary metabolite biosynthesis. Whole-genome resequencing further distinguished ATH from GS115 by only 19 variants (9 SNPs and 10 InDels), highlighting a compact genetic basis for the evolved phenotype. This work provides a K. phaffii chassis with improved individual heat and methanol tolerance and elucidates the physiological, transcriptional, and genomic mechanism underlying heat-methanol cross-adaptation.

title: Liquid contactable colorimetric sensor array for bacteria discrimination.
authors: Kim YM, Lee MG, Kim SH, Shin DI, Lee JH, Kim J, Lim SH, Yi GR
abstract: Rapid and reliable detection of bacterial metabolites in liquid culture is critical for early diagnosis of sepsis, yet conventional dye-based colorimetric sensor arrays (CSAs) are hindered by dye leaching and poor interfacial interactions in aqueous environments. Here, we introduce a polydimethylsiloxane-based CSA (PDMS-CSA) platform that overcomes these limitations by leveraging the intrinsic hydrophobicity of PDMS to stably immobilize water-soluble indicator dyes within the polymer matrix. This design ensures direct, unimpeded contact between analytes and sensors, enhancing both sensitivity and reproducibility. The PDMS matrix further contributes by preventing dye leaching while facilitating mass transport of bacterial metabolites such as ammonia (500 μM), hydrogen sulfide (50 μM), and carbon dioxide (1.7 mM) to the immobilized indicators, thereby enabling rapid and robust colorimetric responses. Using this platform, we achieved reliable differentiation between cocci and bacilli within 3 h, demonstrating a capability for rapid, clinically relevant bacterial identification. By combining operational simplicity with high analytical performance in complex liquid media, PDMS-CSAs represent a transformative approach for point-of-care sepsis diagnostics. Beyond sepsis, this strategy offers a versatile framework for the development of next-generation, non-invasive microbial sensor operating platforms with broad translational potential in clinical and environmental monitoring.

title: Behavioural avoidance to imagined conditioned stimuli in differential fear conditioning.
authors: Mitra S, Lyons AL, Hajiloo M, Greening SG
abstract: The underlying mechanisms of how a fear is born in our imagination is presently unclear. The current study used differential fear conditioning to assess how a fear is created in one's mind and how behavioural avoidance interacts with imagined fear. This study contained an Acquisition, Behavioural Avoidance, and Transfer phase. During the Acquisition phase, participants combined instructions such that whether they heard "imagine yellow" (colour instruction) or "imagine horizontal" (orientation instruction) they were to imagine yellow horizontal lines (CS+) and likewise for the "imagine blue" and "imagine vertical" instructions (CS-). Unbeknownst to participants, they only received the mild shock (US) to the orientation instructions. This manipulation allowed for a disambiguation of descriptive and depictive elements of how imagination interacts with fear. Next, participants completed the Behavioural Avoidance phase, whereby participants had the option to avoid the US after hearing the trial's instructions. Finally, in the Transfer phase, participants were visually shown the CS+ and CS- to determine how their fear transferred from imagery to perception. Self-report, skin conductance response (SCR), and behavioural avoidance attempts were used as dependent measures. Results from each phase and dependent measure suggested that fear was driven by the orientation instructions. Furthermore, fear was shown to transfer from imagery to the corresponding visual stimuli. In this way, these results suggest that both depictive and descriptive elements are involved in the creation of fears in our imagination.

title: Integrated NeutroDrop-enabled single-cell ROS-NE droplet biosensing for sepsis auxiliary diagnosis and survival prediction.
authors: Yao Y, Wang F, Pu X, Shao M, Hua C, Cui J, Zhang Y, Wang Q
abstract: Sepsis assessment relies largely on organ-dysfunction scores and systemic biomarkers, which provide limited information on immune-effector function. We developed NeutroDrop, an integrated droplet microfluidic platform for single-cell profiling of neutrophil reactive oxygen species (ROS)-related oxidative activity and neutrophil elastase (NE)-associated proteolytic activity. Under standardized fMLP stimulation, individual neutrophils were co-encapsulated with fluorescent probes in monodisperse droplets, while membrane-integrity screening and software-assisted image analysis excluded multicell and membrane-compromised droplets. The study included 1012 neutrophils from 10 healthy controls and 2353 neutrophils from 20 patients with sepsis. Analysis of patient-level median signals showed reduced NE activity in sepsis (group means, 28.91 vs. 72.32), whereas ROS showed a nonsignificant decrease (72.14 vs. 92.26). Healthy-reference single-cell analysis revealed marked depletion of high ROS/high NE neutrophils in sepsis (2.89% vs. 16.86%), leading to the PerHighHigh index for healthy/sepsis classification. Local abundance analysis identified a data-derived low-amplitude ROS-NE region associated with non-survival; its patient-level abundance, Pi(R), stratified 12-day outcome with 83.33% sensitivity and 92.85% specificity in the discovery cohort. These locked rules were implemented in NeutroDrop-Plus, which correctly classified all 10 operator-blinded samples and matched 12-day outcomes in 5 of 6 sepsis cases. NeutroDrop converts neutrophil single-cell functional heterogeneity into quantitative biosensing indicators for adjunctive sepsis classification and exploratory short-term outcome stratification.

title: Dissolvable sacrificial interfacial shielding for stable microneedle arrays-based electrochemical dynamic monitoring of sepsis-associated lactate.
authors: Chen WX, Lin CH, Lu YR, Lu TC, Chen ZH, Saqib M, Lei Y, Liu AL
abstract: Continuous lactate dynamic monitoring is essential for timely clinical intervention in sepsis, yet existing serum-based assays are invasive and inherently unsuited for real-time measurement. Microneedle array electrodes (MAEs) enable minimally invasive in situ lactate monitoring in interstitial fluid (ISF); however, mechanical wear at the electrode-tissue interface remains a major obstacle to stable and reproducible analysis. Herein, we report a dissolvable polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP)-shielded MAE for reliable lactate dynamic monitoring. The device integrated an epoxy resin/multi-walled carbon nanotubes microneedle core with a lactate oxidase-gelatin/polythiophene-citrate (LOx-GEL/PEDOT-COO-) sensing interface, combining mechanical robustness, conductivity, biocompatibility, and selective lactate sensing. In artificial ISF, the sensor showed a linear amperometric response from 0.25 to 32 mM with a detection limit of 0.14 mM. Importantly, the dissolvable sacrificial PVP layer was introduced to preserve enzyme activity before use, reduce mechanical abrasion during skin insertion, and subsequently dissolve in situ to enable effective analyte access. In a sepsis-relevant hydrogel skin model, the resulting MAE-based biosensor demonstrated stable and continuous lactate dynamic monitoring, confirming its practical applicability. This dissolvable interfacial shielding strategy provides a versatile design framework for enhancing durability, sensing reliability, and operational safety in microneedle-array enzymatic electrochemical biosensors for ISF biomarker dynamic monitoring.

title: Activatable self-reinforcing nanoplatforms potentiate ferroptosis via starvation and photothermal sensitization for amplified cancer therapy.
authors: Zhao JY, Wang S, Qin K, Wang LJ, Zhang CY
abstract: Tumor microenvironment (TME)-responsive theranostic nanosystems hold considerable promise for cancer therapy. However, converting transient therapeutic effects into sustained and amplified antitumor efficacy remains a challenge due to the absence of dynamic feedback mechanisms in conventional strategies. Herein, we construct an activatable self-reinforcing FeMOF-Au@HA nanoplatform to potentiate ferroptosis via starvation and photothermal sensitization for amplified cancer therapy. This nanoplatform is fabricated through a stepwise strategy by anchoring ultrasmall Au NPs onto FeMOF followed by hyaluronic acid (HA) functionalization. Upon encountering tumor cells, the HA shell binds to CD44 receptors, promoting tumor-targeted accumulation and cellular internalization of FeMOF-AH. After cellular uptake, FeMOF-AH initiates Au-catalyzed glucose oxidation, depleting glucose to induce starvation therapy (ST) and the generation of H2O2. Meanwhile, GSH reduces Fe3+ to Fe2+, facilitating the conversion of H2O2 to ·OH. The subsequent GSH exhaustion and ·OH accumulation disrupt redox equilibrium, inducing glutathione peroxidase 4 inactivation and lipid peroxidation buildup that drive ferroptosis. Ferroptosis further provokes mitochondrial dysfunction, depleting ATP and suppressing heat shock protein 70 (HSP70), thereby attenuating thermotolerance and sensitizing tumors to mild photothermal therapy (PTT, 45 °C). Under 808-nm laser irradiation, mild photothermal heating accelerates glucose oxidation and Fenton catalysis, reinforcing ST and ferroptosis. Notably, ST fuels ferroptosis via metabolite supply, and ferroptosis attenuates thermoresistance to potentiate mild PTT that amplifies oxidative damage, establishing a self-reinforcing therapeutic network. Consequently, FeMOF-AH exhibits enhanced tumor-targeted accumulation by in vivo fluorescence imaging and superior antitumor efficacy over monotherapies with a 92.6% tumor inhibition rate under laser irradiation without systemic toxicity. This nanoplatform offers a new avenue for designing feedback-amplified nanomedicines for durable and enhanced cancer therapy.

title: A fluorinated poly(amino acid) nanovaccine with spatiotemporally encoded innate priming and antigen cross-presentation for tumor immunotherapy.
authors: Wang Z, Su Y, Zhang S, Yu B, Wei Y, Liu H, Veselova IA, Lv S
abstract: The efficacy of cancer vaccines depends on spatiotemporally coordinated innate immune priming and antigen cross-presentation, but this hierarchy remains difficult to control with existing delivery platforms. Here, we report a fluorinated diethylenetriamine-modified poly(aspartic acid) nanovaccine platform, termed DET-F, and identify DET-F30 as the optimized formulation for antigen delivery and immune activation. Perfluorooctyl side chains promote early endosomal toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3) associated innate immune signaling and dendritic cell maturation, whereas the pH-responsive polymer backbone facilitates subsequent endosomal escape and cytosolic antigen release. This chemically encoded sequence enables delayed yet enhanced antigen cross-presentation in mature dendritic cells. DET-F30/antigen nanoparticles display efficient antigen loading and cellular uptake, activate TLR3-related innate immune pathways, and elicit robust antigen-specific CD8+ T cell immunity. In multiple tumor models, DET-F30-based vaccination suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, prolongs survival, and enhances post-surgical anti-PD-1 therapy. This work establishes fluorinated poly(amino acid)s as minimalist self-adjuvant nanovaccine vectors and demonstrates that precise polymer-architecture encoding can orchestrate sequential innate immune activation and antigen processing for improved cancer immunotherapy.

title: Enhanced Esophageal Cancer Detection Using Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer: A Comparative Study of White Light Imaging, Narrow-Band Imaging, and Algorithmic Narrow-Band Imaging-Like Imaging.
authors: Wu JW, Wang YK, Mukundan A, Karmakar R, Nhu NNQ, Nagisetti Y, Liao WC, Han ML
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) detection is crucial for improving survival. While narrow-band imaging (NBI) improves mucosal visualization, limitations remain. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of the Spectrum-Aided Vision Enhancer (SAVE), an algorithmic NBI-like technology reconstructed from white light imaging (WLI). METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, image-based exploratory feasibility study to descriptively evaluate the diagnostic performance of WLI, NBI, and SAVE. A dataset of 1350 still endoscopic images (450 each for WLI, NBI, and SAVE) across normal mucosa, dysplasia, and ESCC stages from 158 patients was blindly reviewed by three endoscopists with different experience levels (3, 5, and 15 years). Diagnostic metrics included sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and reading time. RESULTS: For ESCC, SAVE demonstrated diagnostic performance metrics (sensitivity: 0.81-0.97, specificity: 0.85-0.96) that were numerically similar to WLI and NBI. For dysplasia detection, SAVE had lower observed sensitivity (0.39-0.62) compared to NBI (0.55-0.85) across all observers, representing a clinical limitation for precancerous screening in its current format. Mean per-image reading times were similar across WLI, NBI, and SAVE. CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective study, SAVE showed diagnostic potential for ESCC, with observed diagnostic performance metrics numerically similar to those of WLI and NBI in this exploratory dataset, but lacked sensitivity for dysplasia. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant further prospective, multicenter validation to refine the algorithm for early cancer detection.

title: A climate-driven mechanistic transmission model to characterize dengue epidemiology in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
authors: Paul KK, Regan DG, Green DL, Macadam I, Gray RT
abstract: Dengue is a major public health concern in tropical and sub-tropical areas of the world. Dengue virus is transmitted to humans primarily by female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes and its epidemiology is heavily influenced by the climate. We developed a mechanistic compartmental model to characterize how climate and the evolution of population-level immunity influence changes in the epidemiology of dengue. The model explicitly incorporates aquatic and adult stages of the mosquito vector and cross-immunity (to another serotype) to better represent the transmission of dengue compared to previous models. It incorporates parameters related to mosquito development, behaviour, and mortality that are dependent on temperature, rainfall, and humidity. We calibrated the model to available dengue seroprevalence estimates for Dhaka, Bangladesh as it is a well-observed densely populated endemic area for dengue and will be strongly impacted by climate change. We then simulated dengue epidemiology for the period of 1995-2014 and compared the simulation output with available epidemiologic data. The model produced repeating annual outbreaks of dengue with strong seasonality, as observed in the dengue case reports for Dhaka. The median number of annual dengue infections produced by the model was 1.6 million (IQR: 0.6-2.3 million) and the median of the annual daily peak size of dengue infections was 24,121 (IQR: 7,807-39,308) across the simulations. These figures while exceeding reported cases in Dhaka, which do not include asymptomatic infections or cases not seeking healthcare, align with previous estimates. The modelled seroprevalence of 62% (IQR: 58-75%) aligned with survey results from Dhaka. In most model simulations, dengue infections occurred during August to December with the median peak occurring in October. The model outputs demonstrated a high degree of conformity to the reported data in terms of seasonality, and seroprevalence, indicating that the model provides a good representation of overall dengue epidemiology in Dhaka. By accounting for climate variables, host immunity, and their interplay, our model is well-suited for evaluating the long-term impact of climate change on dengue transmission in Dhaka and other settings where climate and epidemiological data are available.

title: Age-structured two-sex HPV transmission dynamics with a carrier state and reactivation.
authors: Shao S, Guo T, Gao S
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) remains one of the most common sexually transmitted infections worldwide, and its persistence and possible reactivation complicate efforts to understand and control transmission. In particular, the presence of a carrier stage and variation in reactivation across age and sex may play important roles in maintaining HPV prevalence. In this paper, we develop a two-sex Susceptible-Infectious-Carrying-Recovered (SICR) model with n discrete age groups to investigate how age-specific and sex-specific reactivation rates affect HPV transmission dynamics and how control measures can be designed accordingly. We derive the basic reproduction number  R 0   and show that it provides a threshold criterion for disease elimination. The existence and stability of both the disease-free equilibrium and the endemic equilibrium are established rigorously. Using epidemiological data from Hangzhou in 2011, we estimate  R 0   to be 2.177. Analytical and numerical results show that viral reactivation plays an important role in sustaining HPV endemicity and highlight the need for age-specific and sex-specific public health strategies. We also find that an excessively low viral reactivation rate is not always beneficial for controlling HPV prevalence. In particular, regulating reactivation alone is insufficient to control HPV transmission effectively, and our results suggest that combined interventions targeting both transmission and reactivation are more effective.
